stem: In an n-type silicon, which of the following statement is true:

options.label: A
options.text: Electrons are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.

options.label: B
options.text: Electrons are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.

options.label: C
options.text: Holes are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.

options.label: D
options.text: Holes are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.

stem: Which of the statements given in Exercise 14.1 is true for p-type semiconductos.
_note: Two printed oddities, both transcribed as they stand. (1) The book spells it "semiconductos" — its own typo for "semiconductors". (2) The question is a bare CROSS-REFERENCE: the four candidate statements are printed only under Exercise 14.1 and are not repeated here, so this row is not self-contained on /browse the way it is on the printed page. Nothing was added to the stem; the authored solution names the statement in full instead.

subtopic: Classification of Metals, Conductors and Semiconductors
stem: Carbon, silicon and germanium have four valence electrons each. These are characterised by valence and conduction bands separated by energy band gap respectively equal to \((E_g)_{\text{C}}\), \((E_g)_{\text{Si}}\) and \((E_g)_{\text{Ge}}\). Which of the following statements is true?
_note: Option (b) is printed with mixed inequality directions, \((E_g)_{\text{C}} < (E_g)_{\text{Ge}} > (E_g)_{\text{Si}}\), rather than as a single chain. Transcribed exactly as printed; it is a distractor either way.

subtopic: p-n Junction and the Semiconductor Diode
stem: In an unbiased p-n junction, holes diffuse from the p-region to n-region because

options.label: A
options.text: free electrons in the n-region attract them.

options.label: B
options.text: they move across the junction by the potential difference.

options.label: C
options.text: hole concentration in p-region is more as compared to n-region.

subtopic: p-n Junction and the Semiconductor Diode
stem: When a forward bias is applied to a p-n junction, it

options.label: B
options.text: reduces the majority carrier current to zero.

subtopic: Application of Junction Diode as a Rectifier
stem: In half-wave rectification, what is the output frequency if the input frequency is \(50\,\text{Hz}\). What is the output frequency of a full-wave rectifier for the same input frequency.
